items.text: The UN Security Council expressed support for a nationwide ceasefire in Syria, linked to initial political-transition steps, as stated in operative paragraph 5 of Resolution 2254.

evidence.interpretation: The Council requested convening negotiations with a historical target; the text does not establish that talks occurred.

qualifiers.text: with a target of early January 2016

evidence.quote: 2. Requests the Secretary-General, through his good offices and the efforts of his Special Envoy for Syria, to convene representatives of the Syrian government and the opposition to engage in formal negotiations on a political transition process on an urgent basis, with a target of early January 2016 for the initiation of talks, pursuant to the Geneva Communiqué, consistent with the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement, with a view to a lasting political settlement of the crisis;
required_qualifier_literals: with a target of early January 2016

items.text: The Council requested the Secretary-General to convene representatives of the Syrian government and the opposition to engage in formal negotiations on a political transition process, with a target of early January 2016, as stated in operative paragraph 2 of Resolution 2254.

evidence.interpretation: The Council expressed support for an inclusive political process and historical election timetable; this is not an implementation finding.

qualifiers.text: within a target of six months

evidence.quote: 4. Expresses its support, in this regard, for a Syrian-led political process that is facilitated by the United Nations and, within a target of six months, establishes credible, inclusive and non-sectarian governance and sets a schedule and process for drafting a new constitution, and further expresses its support for free and fair elections, pursuant to the new constitution, to be held within 18 months and administered under supervision of the United Nations, to the satisfaction of the governance and to the highest international standards of transparency and accountability, with all Syrians, including members of the diaspora, eligible to participate, as set forth in the 14 November 2015 ISSG Statement;
required_qualifier_literals: within a target of six months

items.text: The Council expressed support for a Syrian-led political process, facilitated by the United Nations, which establishes credible, inclusive, and non-sectarian governance within a target of six months, and sets a schedule and process for drafting a new constitution, as stated in operative paragraph 4 of Resolution 2254.

limitations: This desk note is based on the text of Resolution 2254 and does not reflect current implementation or events on the ground.
The historical timetables mentioned in the resolution, such as the target of early January 2016 for the initiation of talks, are not to be inferred as current deadlines.
questions: What are the key elements of the political transition process outlined in Resolution 2254?
How do the requested negotiations and expressed support for a ceasefire relate to the overall goal of a lasting political settlement in Syria?
